theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is a 'creative brief' for a salon team?
options: A short haircut that the team gives to a model
The bill sent to the client after the event
A written outline of what the client wants
A list of the team's favourite hair products

questions.stem: A bride asks the salon team to style her and six bridesmaids. Which details should the creative brief include?
options: The theme, colours, date, time and budget
The stylists' home addresses and phone numbers
The names of the salon's past wedding clients
The price of every product sold in the salon

questions.stem: Why should the team read the brief together before starting?
options: So each member can change the brief to suit herself
So the client does not need to be asked anything else
So the team can finish faster by skipping planning
So everyone has the same understanding of the goal

questions.stem: Part of the brief is not clear to the team. What should the team leader do?
options: Guess what the client means and start work
Ask the client questions to make it clear
Leave out that part of the brief completely
Let each stylist decide what it means alone

questions.stem: What does a 'deadline' mean in a creative project?
options: The date and time by which work must be ready
The last day a model is allowed to change her mind
The line drawn on a face chart for the brows
The time each day the salon closes its doors

questions.stem: A Carnival band wants bright, bold looks for 20 masqueraders, with one week to prepare. Which part of the brief tells the team how much they can spend?
options: The theme
The timeline
The mood board
The budget

questions.stem: What is 'brainstorming'?
options: Choosing the first idea and sticking to it
Copying a look exactly from a magazine
Sharing many ideas quickly without judging
Asking only the senior stylist for ideas

questions.stem: During brainstorming, Kerry-Ann suggests an unusual idea. What should the team do?
options: Laugh at it so she does not waste their time
Write it down with all the other ideas
Ask her to keep quiet until the end
Tell the client the idea was a bad one

questions.stem: What is a 'mood board'?
options: A board showing staff's moods each day
A notice board that lists the salon's rules
A cleaning chart for all the salon stations
A collage of pictures, colours and textures

questions.stem: Why is a mood board useful to a creative team?
options: It shows everyone the look the team is aiming for
It tells the client how much each stylist will be paid
It replaces the need to talk to each other at all
It lists the products that must be ordered first

questions.stem: Which is a good source of ideas for a hair show on the theme 'Jamaica in the 1960s'?
options: The salon's price list for this year
The product order forms from last month
Old photos and films from that time
The appointment book for next Saturday

questions.stem: What is a 'mind map'?
options: A map showing the way to the event venue
A drawing that links ideas around one theme
A list of the stylists in order of experience
A seating plan for the models backstage

questions.stem: Why should a team look at current trends before planning a look?
options: So the look feels fresh and suits the audience
So they can copy another salon's show exactly
So they never need to make their own decisions
So the look costs as much money as possible

questions.stem: Which is the best way to share your idea in a team meeting?
options: Speak loudly over others so you are heard
Wait until after the meeting and complain
Explain it clearly, with a sketch or photo
Only share it privately with your best friend

questions.stem: Two stylists both want their own idea used for the salon's window display. What is the best way forward?
options: The stylist who argues the loudest should win
Drop both ideas and do nothing at all
Let the stylist who came first decide
Discuss both, and agree or combine them

questions.stem: What does 'compromise' mean in teamwork?
options: Each person refuses to change their mind
Each side gives a little to reach agreement
The leader always makes every choice alone
The team stops working until all agree

questions.stem: Why does a creative team work better when members have different skills, such as braiding, colour and make-up?
options: Because each person can work alone without talking
Because each person adds something the others lack
Because the team then needs no leader or plan
Because it means fewer people need to be trained

questions.stem: What is 'active listening'?
options: Paying full attention and checking you understand
Listening to loud music while you work on the model
Nodding while you think about your own idea
Talking at the same time as the other person

questions.stem: A quiet trainee, Tamika, has not spoken in the planning meeting. What should the team leader do?
options: Ignore her, as she has nothing to add
Tell her she must speak or leave the group
Ask her to make the tea for the meeting
Invite her by name to share her ideas

questions.stem: How can a team keep a record of the ideas agreed at a meeting?
options: Trust everyone to remember them
Ask the client to write them down
Write short notes and share them
Post them on a public social page

questions.stem: Which is an example of constructive feedback?
options: The colours work well. Maybe soften the lip colour.
That look is terrible and you should start over again.
It is fine, I suppose. Do whatever you want.
I would never do it that way. It is wrong.

questions.stem: What is the best way to receive feedback on your design?
options: Argue with each point to defend your work
Ignore it, because it is your own design
Feel upset and stop working on the design
Listen, thank them, and think about it

questions.stem: Feedback on a team member's work should be about:
options: the person's looks and their personality
the work and how it meets the brief
what other people say behind their back
who is the best stylist in the team

questions.stem: When is the best time to give feedback on a practice look?
options: Weeks later, once everyone has forgotten about it
In front of the client, during the event
Soon after the trial, in private or as a team

questions.stem: A team member says your idea will cost too much. What is the best response?
options: Tell her that money does not matter in art
Look for cheaper materials that give a similar look
Use the idea anyway and hide the costs
Leave the team because nobody ever likes your ideas

questions.stem: Why should feedback be specific?
options: So it takes longer to explain to the person
So it sounds more important than it is
So the person feels that they have failed
So the person knows exactly what to change

questions.stem: Why should each member of a creative team have a clear role?
options: So work is not missed or done twice
So members do not need to talk again
So one person can do all of the work

questions.stem: Which is the fairest way to share out roles in the team?
options: Give all the work to the newest trainee
Let the leader do every task by herself
Match tasks to skills and share the load
Give the best tasks to the leader's friends

questions.stem: What is a 'timeline' or 'running order' for a hair show?
options: A list of the prices for each model's look
A line on the floor where the models stand
A plan showing what happens and when
A note of each model's height and size

questions.stem: Seven bridesmaids' hairstyles must be done by 10:00 a.m. Each style takes 1 hour, and 3 stylists work at the same time. What is the latest time they can start if nothing goes wrong?
Why should the team make a list of materials and tools before the event?
options: So they can buy as much stock as they like
So the client can see what the salon owns
So each person brings their own products
So nothing is forgotten on the day

questions.stem: The budget for hair accessories is J$15,000. The team's list comes to J$18,500. What should they do?
options: Change the list or ask the client about more money
Buy everything and hope the client does not notice
Ask each trainee to pay the extra from their pocket
Cancel the whole project and tell no one about it

questions.stem: Which is the best way for a team to keep in touch about changes before an event?
options: Each member waits to hear news on the day
Agree one group message or meeting time
Share changes only with one friend each
Leave notes in different places in the salon

questions.stem: Why does the team do a trial run of the look before the event?
options: To test the look and fix problems in good time
To use up old products that are past their date
To show the client that planning is not needed
To give the model a free service for no reason

questions.stem: During the trial, the hairstyle falls down after 30 minutes. What should the team do?
options: Keep the same style and hope it lasts on the day
Blame the model for moving her head too much
Find out why and change the method or products
Drop the hairstyle from the show with no plan

questions.stem: Why should photos be taken of the trial looks?
options: To post them online before the client agrees
To sell them to a magazine for extra money
To prove which stylist made the mistakes
To compare the looks with the brief later

questions.stem: After the trial, the client asks for softer colours. What should the team do?
options: Refuse, because the plan was agreed already
Make the colours brighter to show their skill
Agree, then make no changes at all on the day
Change the plan and update the mood board

questions.stem: A trainee wants to use a photo from another stylist's online page on a poster for the team's show. What should she do first?
options: Use it, because everything online is free
Change the colours so no one can tell
Ask the owner's permission and give credit
Cut the stylist's name off the photo first

questions.stem: Why should team members give credit for each other's ideas?
options: So nobody ever has to share ideas again
It is fair and builds trust in the team
So the leader can take all of the praise
It means the client pays a higher price

questions.stem: Before photos of a model's finished look are posted on the salon's page, what is needed?
options: The model's agreement, preferably in writing
A good camera and a bright ring light set up
The model's home address and date of birth
Nothing at all, as long as the finished look is nice

questions.stem: The team is planning looks for models with different hair textures and skin tones. What should they do?
options: Use one foundation shade for all of the models
Only choose models with the same hair texture
Treat all hair the same, whatever its texture
Plan products and methods to suit each model

questions.stem: A model will have a bright temporary hair colour for a show. What must be done first?
options: Mix two brands together for a brighter shade
Follow the maker's rules, with any skin test
Apply it straight away to save time on the day
Use it on the scalp even if it is sore and cut

questions.stem: When several people share a make-up kit at a photo shoot, how should lipstick be applied?
options: Straight from the tube onto each model's lips
With the same brush for all models, wiped on a towel
Scraped out with a spatula, then a clean brush
Licked off a finger and dabbed onto the lips

questions.stem: After the event, why should the team hold a review meeting?
options: To learn what went well and what to improve
To decide which member to blame for problems
To plan the payment for the team's next party
To complain about the client behind her back

questions.stem: Which question is most useful in a team review after a show?
options: Who was the slowest stylist on the day?
Which model complained the most backstage?
Why did the other salon look better than us?
Did our looks match the brief and the theme?

essays.stem: A client asks the salon to create hair and make-up looks for a Reggae Month photo shoot. Describe the steps the team should take from first meeting the client to agreeing the final design.
essays.modelAnswer: First the team meets the client to get a clear brief. They ask about the theme, the number of models, the colours and mood she wants, where and when the shoot will be, the budget and the deadline, and they write it all down. If anything is unclear, they ask more questions. Next the team reads the brief together so everyone understands it. They research ideas, for example old reggae album covers, Rastafari colours and current trends, and they brainstorm many ideas without judging. They build a mood board and make sketches or face charts. The team discusses the ideas, gives feedback and agrees on the best ones, combining ideas where possible. They do a trial on a mannequin or a model who agrees, take photos and check them against the brief. Then they present the design to the client, listen to her feedback, make changes, and get her agreement in writing before the shoot.
markingPoints: Meets the client and records a clear brief (theme, models, colours, date, budget, deadline)
Clarifies anything unclear and shares the brief with the whole team
Researches and brainstorms ideas; builds a mood board and sketches
Discusses, gives feedback and agrees on a design; does a trial
Presents to the client, makes changes and gets agreement

essays.stem: Compare two ways a team can come up with ideas for a creative look, such as brainstorming and research for a mood board. Say how each works and when each is useful.
essays.modelAnswer: Brainstorming is when the team sits together and shares as many ideas as possible in a short time. One person writes every idea on chart paper, and nobody judges or laughs at an idea at this stage. Later the team sorts the ideas and picks the best. Brainstorming is quick, gets everyone involved and is useful at the very start of a project, when the team needs many fresh ideas. Research for a mood board means looking at photos, magazines, films, nature, fabrics and trends, and collecting pictures, colours and textures that fit the theme. These are stuck onto a board so the team can see the look and feel. Research takes longer, but it gives the team real examples and helps everyone picture the same result. It is useful once the team has a direction and needs to make it clear. Many teams use both: brainstorm first, then research to build the mood board.
markingPoints: Explains brainstorming: many ideas quickly, recorded, no judging
Says when brainstorming is useful (start of the project, gets everyone involved)
Explains research and mood board: pictures, colours, textures, trends
Says when research is useful (makes the direction clear, shared picture)
Compares them or explains using both together

essays.stem: Explain how to give constructive feedback to a team member about her part of a look, and how to receive feedback on your own work.
essays.modelAnswer: To give constructive feedback, I choose a good time soon after the work, in private or in a team review, not in front of a client. I talk about the work, not the person. I start with something that works well, for example, 'The braids are neat and even.' Then I give one or two clear, specific points to improve and explain why, such as, 'The flowers hide the pattern; could we move them to the side?' I suggest ideas, check that she understood and end on a positive note. To receive feedback, I listen without interrupting or arguing, even if I do not agree at first. I ask questions if I am not clear, thank the person, and think about whether the point helps the look match the brief. Then I use what is useful to improve my work. Taking feedback well shows respect and helps the whole team do better.
markingPoints: Gives feedback at a suitable time and place, about the work not the person
Starts with a strength and gives specific points to improve with reasons
Suggests ideas and checks understanding
Receives feedback by listening without arguing, asking questions and thanking
Uses useful feedback to improve the work against the brief

essays.stem: Two team members strongly disagree about the colour scheme for a show. Describe how the team can settle the disagreement fairly.
essays.modelAnswer: The team leader should stop the argument from becoming personal and call a short meeting at a calm time. Each member explains her idea and her reasons while the others listen without interrupting. The team then goes back to the brief and checks which colours suit the theme, the client, the models' skin tones and the budget. They could put both schemes side by side on the mood board or try both on face charts to see which works better. A compromise is often possible, such as using one member's main colour with the other's accent colour. If the team still cannot agree, they can vote, or the leader or client makes the final choice. Whatever is decided, both members should be thanked for their ideas, and the decision is written down so everyone follows it. Nobody should hold a grudge afterwards.
markingPoints: Keeps it calm and not personal; meets at a suitable time
Each side explains while others listen
Checks both ideas against the brief (theme, client, models, budget)
Tries both, looks for a compromise, or votes or lets the leader or client decide
Thanks both members, records the decision and everyone follows it

essays.stem: Describe how a team of five should share roles and plan the time for styling a bridal party of eight people.
essays.modelAnswer: First the team lists every task: hair for eight people, make-up, accessories, a trial, packing the kit, travel, set-up, touch-ups and clean-up. They match roles to skills, for example two stylists on updos, one on braiding, one on make-up and one as team leader who also does touch-ups and checks the timeline. Work is shared fairly so nobody is overloaded. Next they work out how long each look takes and work backwards from the time the bride must be ready, giving the bride the most time and doing her last or as the client prefers. They add extra time for delays and for travel to the venue. The timeline lists who does whom, and when, on a sheet everyone has. They also make a kit list and agree how to keep in touch, such as one group message. On the day, the leader checks progress against the timeline and moves people to help where a look is running late.
markingPoints: Lists all the tasks, including trial, set-up and clean-up
Matches roles to skills and shares the work fairly
Works out timings backwards from the deadline, with extra time
Writes a timeline everyone can see, with a kit list and a way to keep in touch
Checks progress on the day and adjusts help where needed

essays.stem: Explain why a creative team does a trial run of a look, and how they use the results to improve the design.
essays.modelAnswer: A trial run lets the team test the look before the real event, when there is still time to fix problems. It shows whether the design matches the brief, whether it suits the model's hair texture and skin tone, how long each step really takes, and whether the products and accessories work. It also lets the team check that the model has no reaction to any product, after any skin test the maker requires. During the trial the team takes photos from the front, side and back and writes notes. Afterwards they compare the photos with the brief and the mood board and discuss what worked and what did not. For example, if a style falls down, they may change the pinning method or use a stronger hold product. If it took too long, they change the timeline or add a stylist. They show the trial photos to the client, take her feedback, update the plan and keep a record of the changes.
markingPoints: Tests the look in time to fix problems
Checks the match to the brief, the model, the timings and the products (including reactions)
Takes photos and notes during the trial
Compares with the brief and agrees changes to the method, products or timeline
Gets client feedback and records the updated plan

essays.stem: Explain how team members should respect each other's ideas and other people's work, including photos found online and photos of models.
essays.modelAnswer: Inside the team, every idea should be listened to and written down, even if it is not used. Members should not laugh at ideas or take credit for someone else's idea. When an idea is used, the person who suggested it should be named and thanked. This is fair and builds trust. Outside the team, other people's photos, designs and drawings are protected by copyright. A team can look at them for inspiration, but should not copy a look exactly and call it their own. If they want to use someone else's photo on a poster, a website or social media, they must ask the owner's permission and give credit. Photos of models also need care. The model must agree before photos are taken and before they are posted, preferably in writing. If the model or the Centre does not allow faces to be shown, only the hair or the work area is photographed.
markingPoints: Listens to and records all team ideas, without mocking
Gives credit to the person whose idea is used
Others' photos and designs are protected by copyright: do not copy and claim them
Asks permission and gives credit before using others' work publicly
Gets the model's agreement for photos and posting, and respects limits on faces

essays.stem: Describe the health, safety and hygiene steps a creative team must follow when using hot tools, colour products and shared make-up on models at a show.
essays.modelAnswer: Before the show, the team checks each model for cuts, rashes, scalp problems and allergies, and does any skin test the maker's instructions require for colour products. Colour is used only as the maker says, with gloves, good ventilation and no mixing of brands. Hot tools are checked for damaged cables and plugs, used on a heat mat, tested for heat before they go near the model, and switched off and unplugged when not in use, with cables kept out of walkways. Aerosols are kept away from heat. For hygiene, each model gets a clean towel or cape. Combs and brushes are cleaned and then disinfected between models. Make-up is never used straight from the shared tube or pot: it is taken out with a clean spatula onto a palette and applied with a clean brush or a disposable applicator. Single-use items such as mascara wands are used once and thrown away. Spills are wiped up at once.
markingPoints: Checks models for contraindications and allergies; skin tests as the maker requires
Uses colour as the maker says, with gloves and ventilation, no mixing of brands
Hot tools checked, tested for heat, on heat mats, switched off and unplugged; cables tidy
Clean towels; tools cleaned and disinfected between models
Shared make-up decanted with a spatula; single-use applicators used once

essays.stem: Explain why a creative team gains from members of different ages, backgrounds and skills, and how the team can make sure every member is included.
essays.modelAnswer: People of different ages, backgrounds and skills see things in different ways. An older stylist may know classic styles from the past, a younger one may follow new trends online, and someone from another parish or culture may know other hairstyles, colours or music. One member may be good at braiding, another at colour or make-up, and another at planning. Together they produce more ideas and better solutions than any one person could, and the looks can suit a wider range of clients. To include everyone, the leader can go round the group so each person speaks in turn, and invite quieter members by name. Roles should be shared fairly and matched to skills, with chances for members to learn new ones. All ideas are written down and respected, and nobody is mocked for their background or the way they speak. Decisions are explained so everyone understands them.
markingPoints: Different ages and backgrounds bring different knowledge and ideas
Different skills cover more of the work and solve problems better
Looks can suit a wider range of clients
Includes everyone: turns to speak, inviting quiet members, fair roles
Respects all ideas and backgrounds; no mocking; decisions explained

essays.stem: Describe how a team should review a finished creative project and record what it has learned.
essays.modelAnswer: Soon after the project, while it is fresh in their minds, the team meets for a review. They look at the final photos beside the brief and the mood board and ask: did our looks match the brief, the theme and the budget, and were we ready on time? They collect feedback from the client and, if possible, the models. Each member says what went well and what could be better, about the looks and about how the team worked together, such as communication and sharing of tasks. The leader keeps the talk about the work, not about blaming people. The team writes a short review sheet listing successes, problems, the reasons for them and actions for next time, for example 'do the trial a week earlier' or 'pack spare pins'. The photos, the brief and the review sheet are kept in a project file or portfolio, so the team can use the lessons on the next project.
markingPoints: Holds the review soon after the project
Compares results with the brief, theme, budget and timeline
Collects client and model feedback; each member contributes
Covers teamwork as well as the looks, without blaming
Records successes, problems and actions in a review sheet kept with the photos

practical1.title: Plan a themed look as a team: brief, mood board and design plan
practical1.brief: As a group, plan the hair and make-up looks for an event. The assessor gives you a brief card (for example a Reggae Month photo shoot, an Independence Day fashion show, a church wedding party, or a Christmas window display for the salon) with a theme, number of models, date and a budget. Work in these stages: (1) read the brief together and write down any questions, then ask the assessor, who plays the client; (2) brainstorm on chart paper, with every member adding at least three ideas; (3) build a mood board from magazines, printed pictures, fabric and colour swatches; (4) agree the design by discussion, and write down how any disagreement was settled; (5) each member draws a face chart or hair sketch for one model; (6) write a plan showing roles matched to skills, a timeline that ends at the deadline, a materials list and a budget that stays within the brief; (7) present the plan to the client, with each member explaining one part, then record the client's feedback and make at least one change. Credit any outside picture used on the mood board. Photos show only the boards, sheets and hands, not faces, unless the person agrees and the Centre allows it. Photograph each stage and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: A brief card from the assessor
Chart paper, markers, glue, scissors and sticky notes
Old magazines, printed pictures, fabric and colour swatches
Blank face charts and hair sketch sheets, and coloured pencils
A blank plan sheet (roles, timeline, materials, budget) and a calculator
A phone or camera for photos
photos: The brief card with the team's questions and the answers
The brainstorm sheet with every member's ideas
Each member's face chart or hair sketch
The plan sheet showing roles, timeline, materials and budget
The presentation to the client (boards and hands only)
The updated plan, with the client's feedback and the change made
checklist: Read the brief and asked useful questions to make it clear
Added at least three ideas in the brainstorm and listened to others
Helped build a mood board that fits the theme
Took part in agreeing the design, gave reasons and accepted a fair decision
Produced a clear face chart or hair sketch for one model
Helped write a realistic plan within the budget and deadline
Explained their part of the plan clearly to the client
Gave and received feedback politely and helped make the agreed change
Gave credit for any outside picture used
safety: Use scissors carefully, pass them handle first and put them away after use
Keep the work area tidy, with bags and chairs out of the walkways
Speak respectfully in discussions; no shouting or personal remarks
Plan safe practice in the design: skin tests for colour as the maker requires, and safe use of hot tools

practical2.title: Create a team look on mannequin heads, with a feedback round and review
practical2.brief: As a group, create a matching pair of creative looks on two mannequin heads, from a design the assessor gives you or the one your group planned in Practical 1 (for example a braided updo with accessories for a bridal party, or a bold Carnival style with hair pieces). Work in these stages: (1) set up a clean, safe station and agree roles, so that every member does hands-on work on a head, for example sectioning, braiding, pinning and styling, adding accessories, and checking the finish; (2) section and prepare both heads; (3) work on the looks, checking the design sheet as you go; (4) halfway through, stop for a ten-minute feedback round: each member gives one strength and one improvement for the other head, and the group agrees changes; (5) finish both looks so that they match each other and the design; (6) fill in a team review sheet: what matched the design, what changed and why, and what you would do differently; (7) clean and disinfect tools and leave the station tidy. Photograph each stage and add the photos to the group's practical.
materials: Two mannequin heads with hair, and two clamps or stands
Combs, brushes, section clips, pins, bands and accessories
Hot tools (such as tongs or a flat iron) with heat mats, if the design needs them
Styling products such as gel, mousse or hairspray
The design sheet, a feedback sheet and a team review sheet
Cleaning solution and an approved disinfectant, gloves and a phone or camera
photos: The station set up, with clean tools and the design sheet
Both heads halfway, with the feedback sheet beside them
Both finished looks from the front
Both finished looks from the back and side
The station cleaned, with tools cleaned and disinfected
checklist: Set up a clean station and checked tools and cables before use
Carried out their agreed hands-on part neatly and to the design
Used hot tools safely: tested for heat, rested on a heat mat, switched off and unplugged after use
Gave one clear strength and one improvement in the feedback round
Accepted feedback and helped make the agreed changes
Helped make the two looks match each other and the design
Contributed honest points to the team review sheet
Cleaned, then disinfected, tools and left the station tidy
safety: Check hot tools for damaged cables or plugs before use; keep cables out of walkways
Rest hot tools on heat mats; switch off and unplug them when not in use
Use sprays in a well-ventilated area and keep them away from heat and flames
Keep pins and clips in a tray, not in your mouth; pick up any dropped on the floor
Wear gloves when using disinfectant and follow the maker's instructions for dilution and contact time
